clue.text: It's heard before getting off punishment, caught in plots with politician

indicators.note: something caught in something else is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: plots of garden ground are beds
time is a prison sentence, as in 'doing time'
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician caught in a plot faces punishment, as if a court scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting off' means getting off to sleep, not escaping punishment as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale read aloud to a child in bed is heard just before they drift off to sleep.

clue.text: Saints clad in undies kiss cheek

indicators.note: to be clad in a garment is to be wrapped in it, so the saint goes inside the underwear

parts.note: bras are a kind of undies
S is the standard abbreviation for saint
to neck is to kiss amorously

explanation.surface: A saucy scene of saints in underwear exchanging a kiss on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside BRAS (between the A and the final S) to give BRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass neck is British slang for brazen impudence, which is what cheek means here.

clue.text: Ever fashionable daughter tried to lose weight

parts.note: someone dieting ate less

explanation.surface: A daughter, always stylish, has been dieting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dateless never goes out of date, so it stays timeless in style.

clue.text: Epic account of parliament newspaper brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing letters up means writing them from the bottom, so the run is read backwards

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament
the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs an epic report of a parliamentary session.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem is a long narrative of the Trojan War, an epic by definition.

clue.text: With hair up, French girl meeting king is one putting on a pretty coat

definitions.text: one putting on a pretty coat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a mane is a head of hair
elle is French for she, standing for a girl
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A French girl with her hair up meets a king while putting on a pretty coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'coat' is a coat of enamel, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An enameller applies a glossy decorative layer of enamel to metal or pottery.

clue.text: Smashed head of suction hose

parts.note: smashed and tight are both slang for drunk

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of suction

explanation.surface: A burst hose fixed to the head of a suction pump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' reads as a garden hose but means stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old word for legwear, and tights are legwear covering foot to waist.

clue.text: Hasten to hide US casualty in screen again

indicators.note: one word hiding another holds it inside, out of sight

parts.note: to hasten is to run
ER, the emergency room, is the American name for a hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to conceal an American injury on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeat broadcast, so to rerun a programme is to show it on television once more.

clue.text: Chatterbox knocked back six-pack in silence

indicators.note: placed in means inside the other piece

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, abs

explanation.surface: Someone downs a six-pack of beer in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' and 'six-pack' suggest drinking beer; the six-pack is stomach muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is an informal term for someone who talks endlessly, a chatterbox.

clue.text: Rip off Billy or Jacob's coat

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the woolly coat of a billy goat or a Jacob sheep

explanation.surface: Someone tears off Billy's or Jacob's jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy and Jacob look like men's names; a billy is a male goat and a Jacob is a breed of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is the wool covering an animal, and to fleece is slang for overcharging or cheating.

clue.text: Behind award for actor's moving finale

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is moved to another place, here the front

parts.note: a BAFTA is a British Academy film and television award

explanation.surface: An actor's award won for a moving final scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical term for towards the stern, so behind or aft of something on a ship.

clue.text: Maiden needing cool river around part of summer

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan
August, abbreviated AUG, is a summer month

explanation.surface: A young woman needs a chilly river during the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' is an adjective, as in a maiden voyage or speech, not a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden speech is the first one, and inaugural likewise means first or opening.

clue.text: Was busy with a light that needs fixing?

parts.note: something bust is broken and needs repair
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone was kept busy with a broken lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To bustle is to move about energetically, hurrying with lots of activity.

clue.text: Understanding there's nothing odd about Lennie drinking wine

indicators.note: one drinking another takes it in, so the wine goes inside
with no odd letters left, only the even letters of the name remain

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Nothing unusual about Lennie having a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of Lennie are E, N, E; TENT goes between the N and the last E.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, such as the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Challenge for the ambitious governor disheartened by casual staff

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the first and last letters of governor stay

parts.note: easy means relaxed, casual
a staff is a pole

explanation.surface: A disheartened governor deals with temporary workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual staff' looks like one phrase for temps; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The greasy pole is the hard climb to the top of a career, especially in politics.

clue.text: Person setting up in coalpit, working with earth in the centre?

indicators.note: placed in means inside the anagrammed letters
working means in operation, so the letters are put to work in a new order
in a down clue, up reverses the word

parts.note: the setter of a crossword refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Someone sets up in a coal mine, working the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a descriptive definition: Ptolemy's model of the cosmos put the Earth at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy's astronomical model placed our planet at the heart of the universe.

clue.text: This is coloured, but not evenly

indicators.note: taking no even letters leaves the odd ones, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Something is tinted, but patchily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the clue itself, the thing the solver is reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Every crossword entry has one of these hints, and this line of text is one.

clue.text: One keeps pride in check, changing into more pathetic clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so the outer word goes around

parts.note: lamer means more feeble, more pathetic

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Someone changes into shabbier clothes while keeping their pride under control.
explanation.walkthrough: The pride is a group of lions, not self-esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion tamer controls a group of lions in a circus ring, and a group of lions is a pride.

clue.text: Went to deposit part of capital

parts.note: went means left, departed
to bank money is to deposit it

explanation.surface: Someone went to put money in, as part of their capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank is the southern side of the Seine in Paris, known for artists and cafés.

clue.text: Content to leave awful jelly, one often potted

indicators.note: when the content leaves a word, only its outer letters stay

parts.note: KY Jelly is a brand of lubricant

explanation.surface: Happy to leave a dreadful jelly behind, like a potted plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy, but it means the inside of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alky is slang for an alcoholic, someone often drunk; potted is slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Discrimination in America is set in stone

indicators.note: a jewel set in stone sits inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Prejudice in America is fixed permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against people because of how old they are.

clue.text: Route by either end of Warwick? It gets assessed

parts.note: a course is a route

indicators.note: the alternative word sits by each end letter, flanked on both sides by them
either end of the town's name means just its first and last letters

parts.note: either...or, so either gives or

explanation.surface: A route passing Warwick at either end, assessed like a school project.
explanation.walkthrough: OR goes between the end letters of Warwick, W and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Coursework is school or university work done during a course and marked towards the final grade.

clue.text: Princess penning a recipe, which may involve chops

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the princess holds the other letters

parts.note: Kate is the Princess of Wales
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, take

explanation.surface: A princess writes a recipe that may include lamb chops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chops' suggests meat; it means karate chops.
explanation.definitionFit: This martial art uses sharp hand strikes known as chops.

clue.text: My new beau, naked, is a bit of a looker

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation of surprise like my!

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, the word keeps only its middle

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a new boyfriend, undressed and rather good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A looker' suggests an attractive person; it means an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye, a component of something that looks.

clue.text: Agreed soldiers got into drugs? One won't appeal

indicators.note: something that gets into another goes inside it

parts.note: E is slang for ecstasy, so two doses are Es
yes means agreed
OR, other ranks, refers to soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught taking drugs lose their appeal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' suggests a court appeal; it means being attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, with no visual charm.

clue.text: Anxiety, when taking off top to show boob

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or anxiety

explanation.surface: Anxiety about taking a top off and exposing oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boob' is British slang for a blunder, despite the surface's hint of nudity.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a silly mistake, a blunder.

clue.text: Artist framing outline of outermost hill is Turner

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so RA goes around the other letters

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: an outline is the outer edge, the first and last letters

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill in Devon

explanation.surface: An artist frames the outline of a hill, like the painter Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' wants to be J.M.W. Turner the painter; it is anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that rotates or spins, a turner.

clue.text: Cuban piece of cake with no duplicated ingredients?

indicators.note: the part of the word that appears twice is taken out once

parts.note: a rum baba is a yeast cake soaked in rum syrup

explanation.surface: A slice of cake made without doubling up its ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated BA in RUMBABA appears only once.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a dance and musical style that originated in Cuba.

clue.text: Use force on infamous cyclist when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other

parts.note: Lance Armstrong was stripped of his Tour de France titles for doping

explanation.surface: Someone forcefully confronts a disgraced cyclist during a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To strong-arm someone is to coerce or bully them by force.

clue.text: Let into Duke University after good grade

indicators.note: the university pieces come after the grade

parts.note: A is a top exam grade
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Duke University admits a student after a good grade.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke University is a real US college, but here Duke and University are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit is to allow someone to enter, to let them in.

clue.text: The best solver gets a biscuit

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop
a cracker is someone who cracks puzzles, a solver

explanation.surface: Praise for the top crossword solver who earns a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream cracker is a crisp, unsweetened British biscuit often eaten with cheese.
